structure: Part 3, Dashboard cards, summary and actions. Read in full the eleven dashboard rows of backlog.json increments[] by their line ranges: inc-014 (1383-1564), inc-015 (1842-2003), inc-016 (2004-2141), inc-002 (2448-2646), inc-025 (2647-2778), inc-026 (27772-27986), inc-030 (30774-30905), inc-031 (30906-31196), inc-027 (31197-31328), inc-028 (31329-31472) and inc-029 (31473-31605). Each row carries title, detail, finding {frontend, prototype, difference, correction or verification, falsifiedBy, relatedTo}, citations, controls, provenance and a decision. Nine rows are status blocked with decision.ruling "block" and an identical decision.note (Rhys, 2026-08-28: the dashboard is temporary in the animals frontend and moves to trade-imports-ins-frontend); two (inc-030, inc-031) are status dropped with decision.ruling "reject" by Sam on 2026-08-21 and a ruledAt timestamp. Claims cover, for every row, the ruling, who ruled and when, and the reason; then the difference each row judged, its band, and any open question or rule the row states. Provenance notes on how runs A and C were matched, citations and screens were read for context and not claimed as judgements.

claims.ref: backlog.json increments[] inc-014 (and the eight other blocked rows of this part): decision.note
claims.quote: Deferred, not rejected — if the dashboard stays, these need a fresh ruling rather than a re-raise.

claims.statement: The 2026-08-28 dashboard blocks join inc-023 and inc-024, which were blocked earlier on the same grounds.
claims.ref: backlog.json increments[] inc-014 (and the eight other blocked rows of this part): decision.note

inc-014 (blocked): the frontend dashboard has no "At a glance" summary, while DR1 opens the dashboard with one showing counts of alerts, errors and messages waiting for the trader.
claims.quote: The dashboard shows no "At a glance" summary; Design release 1 opens it with counts of alerts, errors and messages waiting for the trader

claims.statement: inc-014: DR1 shows, between the start button and the notification list, a section headed "At a glance" with three cards (Alerts, Errors, Messages), each with an icon, a count and a link "View alerts", "View errors" or "View messages".
claims.quote: Between the start button and the notification list Design release 1 shows a section headed "At a glance" holding three cards side by side: Alerts, Errors and Messages (app/views/dashboard.html:39-77). Each card shows an icon, a count, and a link — "View alerts", "View errors", "View messages" — that takes the trader to the detail.

claims.statement: inc-014: in DR1 the alert, error and message counts are hard-coded to zero and every link is an href="#" placeholder, so DR1 does not say what the three lists contain.
claims.quote: The counts come from the view model's alertCounts, which hard-codes {alerts: 0, errors: 0, messages: 0} for every release (app/routes.js:7207-7211), so all three read 0 in the capture, and every link is an href="#" placeholder. The design states that the three lists exist and are reachable but not what they contain

claims.statement: inc-014 is banded needs-backend: no service in the workspace exposes alert, error or message counts for the signed-in organisation, and the notification contract does not carry them.
claims.ref: backlog.json increments[] inc-014: band and finding.difference
claims.quote: a source of alert, error and message counts for the signed-in organisation, which no service in this workspace exposes today and which the notification contract does not carry

claims.statement: inc-014 leaves open what an alert, an error and a message are, and what the three destination pages show, because DR1 shows the categories but not their contents.
claims.quote: a decision on what an alert, an error and a message are, since Design release 1 shows the categories and not their contents; and the three destination pages the links point at, which Design release 1 leaves as placeholders.
claims.note: The row states the open question; the source does not answer it.

claims.statement: inc-014 judges that the "At a glance" section can be built showing zero counts before the counts exist, but is not worth shipping until the counts are real.
claims.quote: The section itself can be built and shown with zero counts before any of that lands, so the visual work does not have to wait, but the section is not worth shipping until the counts are real.

claims.statement: inc-015 (blocked): the frontend dashboard notification card shows the reference and eight labelled facts over three rows (Commodity, Origin, Arrival at destination; Consignee, Consignor, Status; Date created, Date submitted).
claims.quote: A notification card carries its reference as a heading and then eight labelled facts in three rows of three: Commodity, Origin, Arrival at destination; Consignee, Consignor, Status; Date created, Date submitted

claims.statement: inc-015: DR1's notification card shows the reference and four facts over two rows: Commodity and Status first, then Origin and "Arrival date at destination"; consignee, consignor and the created and submitted dates are not shown.
claims.quote: Design release 1's card carries the reference and four facts in two rows of two: Commodity and Status on the first row, Origin and "Arrival date at destination" on the second (app/views/dashboard.html:265-292). Consignee, consignor and the created and submitted dates are not shown.

claims.statement: inc-015 proposed cutting the card to DR1's four facts and explicitly left which links the card offers as a separate question; the proposal is blocked.
claims.ref: backlog.json increments[] inc-015: finding.difference and decision
claims.quote: Cut the card down to the four facts the design shows, in the design's order and layout ... Which links the card offers is a separate question and is not changed here.

claims.statement: inc-015: DR1's card identifies a consignment by what is coming, from where and when, and leaves the parties (consignee, consignor) to the notification itself.
claims.quote: Design release 1's card identifies a consignment by what is coming, from where and when, and leaves the parties to the notification itself.

claims.statement: inc-015: on a draft card in the frontend, five of the eight facts are blank (Commodity, Arrival at destination, Consignee, Consignor and Date submitted), so the card is mostly empty labels.
claims.quote: On a draft, five of the eight are blank — the picture of fe-dashboard-populated shows Commodity, Arrival at destination, Consignee, Consignor and Date submitted all empty — so the card is mostly labels with nothing beside them.

claims.statement: inc-016 (blocked): the date on a dashboard card is labelled "Arrival at destination" in the frontend and "Arrival date at destination" in DR1.
claims.quote: DR1 labels the date on a notification card "Arrival date at destination"; the frontend labels it "Arrival at destination".

claims.statement: inc-016 was meant to be done in the same pass as inc-015, because both edit the same card copy block.
claims.ref: backlog.json increments[] inc-016: finding.difference and finding.relatedTo
claims.quote: Do it in the same pass as cutting the card down to DR1's four pairs, raised as inc-015, since both edit the same copy block

claims.statement: inc-016 would change the card's arrival label in both the English and Welsh dashboard copy files.
claims.quote: Change the label to "Arrival date at destination" in the English and Welsh copy files for the dashboard feature.

claims.statement: inc-002 (blocked): the frontend dashboard's browser title reads "Import notification service | Import notification service", while DR1 names the page "Dashboard".
claims.quote: The dashboard's browser tab reads "Import notification service | Import notification service"; Design release 1 names the page "Dashboard"

claims.statement: inc-002: DR1 names the page "Dashboard" in three places (the browser tab, the caption above the heading, and the active service navigation item) while the h1 stays "Import notification service"; the DR1 tab reads "Dashboard - Import notification service - GOV.UK".
claims.quote: Design release 1 names the page "Dashboard" and shows the same word as the caption above the heading, while the heading itself stays "Import notification service" (app/views/dashboard.html:12). The tab reads "Dashboard - Import notification service - GOV.UK". The same word is also the active item in the service navigation bar

claims.statement: inc-002 proposed a page name "Dashboard" with the h1 kept as the service name, and said it should travel with the separate title-format finding (inc-011); the proposal is blocked.
claims.ref: backlog.json increments[] inc-002: finding.difference and finding.relatedTo
claims.quote: Give the dashboard a page name of its own — "Dashboard" — and keep the h1 as the service name, which is what the design does.

claims.statement: inc-002: the frontend's dashboard title repeating the service name means a trader with several tabs open cannot tell the dashboard from other pages, and a screen reader announces the service name twice.
claims.quote: A trader with several tabs open cannot tell the dashboard from any other page of the service, and a screen reader announces the service name twice.

claims.statement: inc-002 leaves the title separator and the absence of a "GOV.UK" suffix out of question; only the dashboard's page name is in question.
claims.quote: The separator and the absence of a "GOV.UK" suffix are not in question here; only the page name is

claims.statement: inc-025 (blocked): the frontend dashboard's entry action is a GOV.UK start button reading "Start a new notification"; DR1 uses a standard button reading "Create a new notification".
claims.quote: The dashboard's button to begin a notification reads "Start a new notification" and is a GOV.UK start button; Design release 1 uses a standard button reading "Create a new notification"

claims.statement: inc-025 judged that the frontend creating a notification with a form POST, against DR1's link, is an implementation difference outside the change.
claims.quote: The form around it stays: the frontend creates the notification with a POST and Design release 1 uses a link, which is an implementation difference and not part of this change.

claims.statement: inc-025: DR1's "Create a new notification" button sits directly under the heading, with no start-button icon and no extra height, so it reads as one action on a signed-in landing page rather than the front door to the service.
claims.quote: Design release 1 shows a standard button reading "Create a new notification" directly under the heading (app/views/dashboard.html:32-36). It carries no start-button icon and no extra height, so it reads as one action among several on a signed-in landing page rather than as the front door to the service.

claims.statement: inc-026 (blocked): the frontend lets a user delete a notification and cancel an amendment from dashboard cards; DR1 has neither journey reachable at its root.
claims.quote: The frontend lets a user delete a notification and cancel an amendment from the dashboard; DR1 has neither journey, and whether they are in scope for DR1 parity is unsettled.

claims.statement: inc-026: the frontend's delete confirmation is headed "Delete this notification?", says "This cannot be undone.", and offers a red "Yes, delete notification" and "No, return to dashboard"; it is reached from a card's Delete action and from the Delete button on a submitted notification's read-only review page.
claims.quote: Delete leads to a confirmation page headed "Delete this notification?" saying "This cannot be undone." with a red "Yes, delete notification" and "No, return to dashboard"; it is reached both from the Delete action on a dashboard card and from the Delete button at the top of a submitted notification's read-only review page.

claims.statement: inc-026: the frontend's cancel-amendment confirmation is headed "Cancel this amendment?", says the changes since amending started will be discarded and the submitted version restored, and offers "Yes, cancel amendment" and "No, return to notification".
claims.quote: Cancel amendment leads to "Cancel this amendment?" saying the changes since amending started will be discarded and the submitted version restored, offering "Yes, cancel amendment" against "No, return to notification".

claims.statement: inc-026: in the DR1 prototype the delete and cancel-amend pages exist only under design-release-2 and design-release-2.1, and are guarded so a root-mount (DR1) session is redirected to the dashboard.
claims.quote: the delete page redirects to the dashboard unless the session carries the design-release-2 flag (app/routes.js:5607-5613), and cancel-amend does the same (app/routes.js:9652-9655) ... there is no delete-notification.html and no cancel-amend.html at the root of app/views, only copies under design-release-2/ and design-release-2.1/

claims.statement: inc-026 is banded disputed: it is unsettled whether delete and amend were in DR1's scope; only a statement from the designer settles it.
claims.ref: backlog.json increments[] inc-026: band and finding.difference
claims.quote: What settles it is a statement from the designer on whether delete and amend were in the DR1 scope: if they were, DR1's dashboard card is missing a Delete action and the absence is a prototype gap; if they were not, both frontend journeys are ahead of the signed-off design and belong to the next comparison.
claims.note: Open question recorded by the row, not answered by it.

claims.statement: inc-026 instructs that, until the designer settles scope, the frontend's delete and cancel-amendment pages are treated as unassessed rather than as defects, and nothing is raised about their copy, button pattern or confirmation wording.
claims.quote: Until then, treat the two frontend pages as unassessed rather than as defects, and raise nothing about their copy, their button pattern or their confirmation wording.

claims.statement: inc-026 notes that the delete and amend journeys may be design-release-2 features that shipped early in the frontend, in which case they belong to a DR2 comparison rather than DR1.
claims.ref: backlog.json increments[] inc-026: finding.difference and finding.correction
claims.quote: Either delete and amend are design-release-2 features that shipped early in the frontend, in which case they are out of scope here
claims.note: One of two readings the row offers; it does not choose.

claims.statement: inc-026: submitted cards in the frontend also offer Amend, which is where an amendment that can be cancelled comes from; Cancel amendment appears only on a card being amended.
claims.ref: backlog.json increments[] inc-026: finding.frontend and finding.correction
claims.quote: Submitted cards also offer Amend, which is where the amendment being cancelled comes from.

claims.statement: inc-026: DR1's dashboard card offers only Copy as new and View.
claims.quote: The card offers Copy as new and View and nothing else (app/views/dashboard.html:257-262)

claims.quote: So disputed is the right band and the designer's answer changes what this belongs to, not what anyone builds.

claims.statement: inc-030 (rejected): DR1 gives every card the same two links, "Copy as new" then "View", whatever the status, and its View opens the review page for a draft as well as a submitted notification.

claims.quote: There is no way to look at a draft without re-entering it: Resume goes to the task list (`hubPath`) and View exists only once the notification has been submitted, when it opens Check your answers.

claims.statement: inc-031 (dropped) was rejected by Sam on 2026-08-21, upgrading an earlier deferral that day: the frontend keeps its always-sorted dashboard and DR1's unselected sort control ("Select one") is not adopted.
claims.ref: backlog.json increments[] inc-031: decision.ruling, decision.note, decision.ruledAt (2026-08-21T12:08:09Z)
claims.quote: Carried from run C inc-098, rejected by Sam on 2026-08-21, upgrading that day's earlier deferral. Keep the frontend's always-sorted dashboard; Design release 1's unselected sort control is not to be adopted.

claims.statement: The reason given for rejecting inc-031 is that the dashboard is temporary, so no sort work is wanted.
claims.quote: The dashboard is temporary, so no sort work is wanted.

claims.statement: The frontend dashboard always has an ordering applied, defaulting to "Arrival (newest to oldest)" (sort arrivalDate,desc) on an untouched page, and every notification list request carries a sort parameter.
claims.quote: the picture of fe-dashboard-populated shows "Arrival (newest to oldest)" already selected on a page the trader has not touched. The default is carried all the way to the notification list read, which defaults the parameter again and interpolates it unconditionally into the request
claims.note: The arrivalDate,desc default is named in finding.difference: "defaults sort to arrivalDate,desc".

claims.statement: inc-031 records that neither DR1 nor the prototype says what order the notifications API returns with no sort parameter; the prototype list is in fixture order whatever its select says.
claims.ref: backlog.json increments[] inc-031: finding.prototype and finding.difference
claims.quote: confirm with the notifications API's owners what order it returns when no sort parameter is sent before this ships, because that order is what a trader will actually see and neither this design nor the prototype specifies it.
claims.note: Moot while the rejection stands; recorded because the row states it.

claims.statement: inc-031 (rejected): DR1's sort select loads on an unselected "Select one" placeholder ahead of three orderings (Newest first, Oldest first, Arrival date).

claims.quote: Select one (selected), Newest first, Oldest first, Arrival date

claims.statement: inc-027 (blocked): DR1's dashboard shows a "Submitted action required" status on submitted notifications that still need something from the user; the frontend card can only show its own journey states (Draft, Submitted, Amending or Deleted).
claims.quote: DR1's dashboard tells a user which submitted notifications still need something from them with a "Submitted action required" status; the frontend can only ever say Draft, Submitted, Amending or Deleted.
claims.note: finding.correction says Deleted is unreachable on the dashboard because deleted rows are filtered out, so the card in practice shows Draft, Submitted or Amending.

claims.statement: inc-027: DR1's status filter names seven statuses: Draft, Submitted, In progress, Approved, Action required, Rejected and Complete.
claims.quote: DR1's status filter names a wider set again — Draft, Submitted, In progress, Approved, Action required, Rejected and Complete

claims.ref: backlog.json increments[] inc-027: band and finding.difference
claims.quote: So the record contract needs a status the authorities can set, and the list read has to return it, before the tag can be added and the status filter built on top of it.

claims.statement: inc-027 leaves the full set of post-submission status values to be agreed against what the service really reports, not copied from the prototype fixture, since DR1 names seven in the filter but shows only three on cards.
claims.quote: Agree the full set of values at the same time — DR1 states seven in the filter but only demonstrates three on cards, so the list has to be settled against what the service really reports rather than copied from the prototype fixture.
claims.note: Open question recorded by the row.

claims.statement: inc-027: on DR1's dashboard, two of the four cards carry an orange "Submitted action required" tag and two a green "Submitted" tag.
claims.ref: backlog.json increments[] inc-027: finding.prototype and finding.correction
claims.quote: Two of the four cards on DR1's dashboard carry an orange "Submitted action required" tag beside the green "Submitted" of the others

claims.statement: inc-027: the frontend's status tags are Draft (blue), Submitted (green), Amending (yellow) and Deleted (grey), and once submitted a notification reads Submitted and stays that way.
claims.quote: The status tag on a card comes from a fixed map of four journey states: Draft (blue), Submitted (green), Amending (yellow) and Deleted (grey) (src/server/app/shared/kit.js:34-51). Once a notification is submitted it reads Submitted and stays that way

claims.statement: inc-027's verifier records that the frontend dashboard strips deleted notifications from the list before cards are built, so the grey Deleted tag never shows there.
claims.quote: on the dashboard it can only ever say Draft, Submitted or Amending — the controller strips deleted rows out of the list before the cards are built

claims.statement: inc-028 (blocked): the frontend dashboard lists drafts with a Draft tag and a Resume link to the task list; DR1's dashboard never shows a draft, though its status filter offers Draft.
claims.quote: The frontend's dashboard lists a draft so the user can resume it; DR1's dashboard cannot show a draft at all, while its own status filter offers Draft as something to filter by.

claims.statement: inc-028: DR1's dashboard list drops both drafts and submission-complete records before rendering, so four of its eight fixture notifications never appear and the page reads "Show 1-4 of 4 results".
claims.ref: backlog.json increments[] inc-028: finding.prototype and finding.correction
claims.quote: that view drops every record marked as a draft and every record marked as submission-complete. The DR1 fixture holds eight notifications, two of them drafts and two of them completed, and only the remaining four ever appear — which is why the page reads "Show 1-4 of 4 results".

claims.statement: inc-028 is banded disputed: whether a draft is meant to appear on the DR1 dashboard needs a designer's answer; the row judges the exclusion more likely an accident of shared later-release code.
claims.ref: backlog.json increments[] inc-028: band and finding.difference
claims.quote: What settles it is a designer saying whether a draft is meant to appear on the DR1 dashboard. ... The accident reading is the more likely one on the evidence
claims.note: Open question recorded by the row, with a stated leaning but no answer.

claims.statement: inc-028 judges that if drafts are not meant to be on the dashboard, the frontend needs a stated home for drafts before anything is removed, because resuming a draft from the dashboard is the only way back into an unfinished notification.
claims.quote: If it is not, the frontend's dashboard needs a stated home for drafts before anything is removed from it, because resuming a draft is the only way back into an unfinished notification today.

claims.statement: inc-028: in the frontend a draft card's Resume link takes the user back to the notification's task list.

claims.quote: Nothing in the root design offers a way to see the other four: the root view renders no tabs and no link anywhere carries a tab, and the tab links the shared code builds all point at the design release 2.1 dashboard rather than at this one.

claims.statement: inc-028 says that if drafts are meant to be off the DR1 dashboard, the Draft option should come off the status filter and the design owes an answer to where a user resumes unfinished work.
claims.quote: Either the dashboard is deliberately a list of live consignments and drafts belong somewhere else, in which case the design owes an answer to where a user resumes unfinished work and the Draft option should come off the status filter
